newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil pension funds not bidding at CVRD auction.
newsitem.headline: Brazil pension funds not bidding at CVRD auction.

text.p: Brazilian pension funds will not bid at the privatization of state mining company CVRD, but plan to join the winning consortium afterwards, said a director of the Brazilian association of pension funds, Abrapp.
A strategic 45 percent of CVRD voting shares is being aunctioned on April 29 on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange for a base price of three billion reais ($2.83 billion).
"We do not intend to allocate new funds (in CVRD). We already have 15 percent," said Abrapp Economic and Financial Director Ildemar Almeida da Silva.
"The idea is to negotiate a deal with the winning bidders which preserves the interests of the pension funds."
Silva said the pension funds felt no need to help finance any of the CVRD consortia because their existing stakes already gave them enough bargaining power.
Pension funds jointly hold 15 percent of CVRD's voting stock and 18 percent of CVRD's total capital.

The pension funds were negotiating as a group with the two consortia forming around Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and Brazil's largest steelmaker, Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN).
In exchange for their support of the winning consortium the pension funds want a seat on CVRD's board of directors once the company is privatized, Silva said.

He said the pension funds were also talking with CVRD's employees, who will be able to acquire 4.45 percent of CVRD's voting shares and six percent of the preference shares under the privatization rules. The new owners of the 45 percent voting block will be in a controlling position once they team up with the pension funds and the CVRD employees.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
